profile.address: San Diego, CA (LightEdge publishes two addresses in this market, 9305 Lightwave Avenue and 9725 Scranton Road, exact SAN1 match unconfirmed)
profile.reading:
LightEdge SAN1 sits in San Diego, California. LightEdge's own site publishes two distinct San Diego street addresses for its market presence there, 9305 Lightwave Avenue in the 92123 zip code and 9725 Scranton Road in the 92121 zip code, on different streets in different parts of the city. Nothing in LightEdge's public materials assigns the SAN1 label to one address over the other, so this record treats both as unconfirmed candidates rather than guessing at a match.

Per LightEdge's own combined specification sheet for the San Diego market, current as of a March 2026 revision, the two buildings together provide 2.9 megawatts of critical IT workload capacity and 10 megawatts of total generator capacity, running an N plus 1 UPS configuration, across 100,000 total square feet that includes 56,342 square feet of raised floor whitespace. The same sheet lists thirteen on net carriers serving the combined footprint, among them AT&T, Cogent, Comcast, Lumen, NTT, Verizon and Zayo, and a certification set spanning SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 audits, ISO 20000-1, ISO 22301 and ISO 27001, HITRUST and HIPAA and HITECH readiness, PCI DSS, and both NIST 800-53 and NIST 800-171 controls, a compliance heavy stack aimed at regulated enterprise tenants rather than hyperscale cloud customers.

LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. In September 2021 the company announced a capital partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm whose earlier ventures include founding Digital Realty in 2004, with then CEO Jim Masterson stating publicly that the deal would change neither management, operations, nor customer facing teams. Masterson led LightEdge for 21 years before moving to an advisory board seat at the end of 2024, and Rob Carter succeeded him as CEO on January 1, 2025. LightEdge now describes its national footprint as 20 data centers across 12 United States metro markets plus one location in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, with San Diego serving as one of the smaller markets in that portfolio.

San Diego has grown into a secondary California data center hub in part because it sits outside the more expensive, power and land constrained Silicon Valley corridor, drawing enterprise and healthcare tenants who want a California presence without competing for scarce interconnection capacity in San Jose or Santa Clara. No source located this session discloses a year built, tier rating, or named tenant for either San Diego address, and LightEdge does not publish a named utility provider for the market on its own site, though San Diego Gas and Electric is the incumbent electric utility serving both zip codes in question.

reading.body:
LightEdge's San Diego market presence totals 2.9 megawatts of critical IT workload capacity across two addresses whose exact assignment to the SAN1 facility code remains unconfirmed by LightEdge's public materials. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, this translates to roughly 73 racks. The 10 megawatts of total generator capacity and N plus 1 UPS configuration provide redundancy for continuous operation, though the published workload figure is the binding constraint on current capacity.

The certification stack spanning SOC audits, ISO standards, HITRUST, HIPAA readiness, and NIST controls signals this campus is built for regulated enterprise and healthcare tenants rather than hyperscale AI workloads. Thirteen named carriers including AT&T, Comcast, Lumen, NTT and Verizon serve the footprint, establishing baseline connectivity but not published direct interconnection to cloud GPU clusters. The 56,342 square feet of raised floor whitespace provides room for tenant expansion within the stated megawatt envelope.

San Diego ranks twelfth among California facilities with published capacity figures and represents less than 1 percent of the state's 365 published megawatts. LightEdge operates this location as part of a 20-facility national portfolio focused on secondary metropolitan markets where enterprise demand exists outside Silicon Valley's constrained power and land availability. The campus does not appear positioned as a primary AI training destination in its current published configuration.
